comment: Senate Class II seats (last elected 2020), plus OH and FL special elections. dem_seats_not_up / rep_seats_not_up reflect current composition minus seats being contested.

races.note: Tommy Tuberville running for governor instead. Open R primary: Steve Marshall (AG), Barry Moore (Rep), Jared Hudson among leading candidates. Deep-red state remains Safe R.

Mary Peltola (former congresswoman, lost House seat 2024) challenging Sullivan. Ranked-choice voting. 8 polls (Jul '25–Mar '26) avg D+3.7. Race has trended toward Peltola: Alaska Survey Research (Mar '26): D+5.5 and D+4.8 in paired questions — strongest results yet. Earlier polls showed R+4 (Aug '25) trending to D+2 by Jan '26. Alaska has a history of electing crossover candidates. Now a toss-up.
Cotton seeking third term in deep-red Arkansas. Democrat Hallie Shoffner, a farmer and first-time candidate, won the D primary. Cotton's 33.6-pt 2020 margin and R+24 PVI make this Safe R.

Hickenlooper seeking re-election (says this will be his final Senate term). Faces a D primary challenge from state Sen. Julie Gonzales. No major R challenger has emerged. Colorado has shifted solidly blue at the federal level. Safe D.
Coons running for a fourth term in deep-blue Delaware. R primary features only minor candidates. No Republican has won a Senate race in Delaware since 1994. Safe D.

Vacancy election for Marco Rubio's vacated seat, on the November 2026 midterm ballot alongside all other races. Ashley Moody (R, former FL AG) appointed. D primary: Vindman, Nixon, Mujica. 10 polls avg R+4.4. Vindman polls best among D candidates; most polls show Moody ahead R+7 to R+11. Two recent outliers pull the avg toward competitive: MDW (Apr '26, unrated) R+1; Change Research (May '26, D-leaning) D+2 vs field of R+7 to R+11. Cherry Communications (May '26, R-sponsored): R+8.

Won by 1.2% in January 2021 runoff; top Republican target in 2026. R primary held May 19 — results pending in data. 14 polls across 8 pollsters avg D+7.1 vs likely R nominees. Ossoff leads all tested R candidates. Most recent: Echelon (Apr '26): Ossoff D+7 vs Collins, D+9 vs Carter. Emerson (Mar '26): D+3 to D+8. Top D incumbent defense seat.
Risch (age 83 at election) confirmed running for re-election with Trump's endorsement. Faces minor R primary challengers and a weak D field. Deep-red Idaho (R+32) keeps this Safe R.

Dick Durbin retiring. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the D primary (March 17) with 40% over Krishnamoorthi and Kelly. Former IL GOP chair Don Tracy won the R primary. Stratton is heavily favored in deep-blue Illinois.

Joni Ernst retiring. R primary June 3: Hinson heavily favored over Carlin. D primary June 3: Wahls vs Turek (competitive primary). Echelon (Apr '26): Wahls D+2, Turek D+1 vs Hinson — closest polling of cycle. GBAO (Mar '26, D-sponsored): Wahls R+3, Turek R+4. Change Research (Jan '26): R+3 across D candidates. Iowa has trended solidly R but race is closer than PVI suggests.

Marshall seeking re-election with only minor R primary opposition. D primary Aug 4 — Patrick Schmidt emerging as leading D candidate. GQR (Apr '26, D-sponsored): Schmidt R+4. Tavern Research (Jan '26): generic D R+8. Deep-red Kansas (R+20) keeps this Safe R regardless of D nominee.

Mitch McConnell retiring after 42 years. R primary: Rep. Andy Barr, former AG Daniel Cameron, Nate Morris. D candidate: Charles Booker. PPP polls (D-sponsored, Dec '25) show Morris only +1 vs Booker, Cameron +7, Barr +11. Avg vs named R candidates: R+6.3. If Morris wins the R primary, this could be more competitive than PVI suggests — but R+26 keeps it Safe R.

Cassidy faces a serious R primary challenge from Rep. Julia Letlow, who has Trump's endorsement, due to Cassidy's vote to convict Trump in his second impeachment trial. Former Rep. John Fleming also running. D field is weak. Louisiana remains Safe R regardless of primary outcome.

Collins is a moderate R who historically outperforms PVI by 10+ pts. D primary June 10: Platner vs Mills. Platner leads Collins in 12 of 14 tested matchups, avg D+5 (range: even to D+11); Pan Atlantic (May '26): Platner D+7 — latest. Mills trails Collins in most polls, avg near even. If Platner wins primary, this is a genuine toss-up trending D; if Mills, Collins likely holds. 15 polls in window avg D+3.6 (all candidate matchups).

Markey (age 80) seeking a third full term. Rep. Seth Moulton is mounting a significant D primary challenge on generational change. Polls show Markey leading Moulton by 13-23 pts. No credible R challenger in D+30 Massachusetts. Safe D.

Gary Peters retiring. D primary Aug 2026: McMorrow, Stevens, El-Sayed. R candidate Mike Rogers. 8 polls in window avg R+2.3. May '26 polls (Glengariff, Mitchell) show Rogers R+2 to R+3 across all D candidates — race has stabilized with Rogers advantage. Stevens polls best (avg R+0.5 in Jan Emerson), McMorrow middle, El-Sayed weakest. Primary outcome will determine competitiveness.

Tina Smith retiring. D primary (Aug 2026): Flanagan leads Craig by 3–30 pts in early polls. R candidate: Michele Tafoya. Emerson (Feb '26) shows both Flanagan and Craig at ~D+6.5 vs Tafoya. PPP (Sep '25) showed D+2 to D+4 vs generic R. Minnesota leans D.
Hyde-Smith won the R primary (March 10) with 81%. She faces Democrat Scott Colom, Lowndes County DA. No Democrat has won a MS Senate race since 1982. Safe R.

Steve Daines withdrew minutes before filing deadline and endorsed Kurt Alme (U.S. attorney). Controversial last-minute maneuver designed to clear the R primary field. Tavern Research (May '26): Generic Dem R+12, Reilly Neill R+16 vs Alme — confirms deep R lean despite open seat. Montana remains solidly R.

Dan Osborn (Independent) challenging Ricketts, who was appointed in 2023 after Ben Sasse resigned. Osborn nearly beat Deb Fischer in 2024, running ~10 pts ahead of PVI as a populist Independent. Tavern Research (May '26): Osborn D+5 vs Ricketts; Impact Research (Feb '26, D-sponsored): Osborn R+1 adjusted. Osborn-specific poll avg D+4.2. Note: NE's R+22 PVI heavily offsets this in the fundamentals blend — model win probability (~13%) likely understates Osborn's actual chances given his Independent appeal. Osborn would likely caucus with Democrats. Modeled on D side.

Jeanne Shaheen retiring. Pappas (D) vs Sununu (R) is the competitive matchup: 13 polls avg D+4 (range: D+2 to D+6). UNH (Apr '26): Sununu D+5 — slight improvement from Emerson Mar '26 D+2. Pappas dominates Brown matchup at D+10+ avg. Sununu filing deadline approaching — if he enters, this is a top-tier battleground. If Brown wins primary, likely D hold.
Booker seeking a third full term. R primary features only minor candidates. NJ has not elected a Republican senator since 1972. Safe D.
Only GOP candidate (Christopher Vanden Heuvel) disqualified for insufficient petition signatures. No Republican will appear on the general election ballot — first time in modern NM history.

Thom Tillis not seeking re-election; open seat. Roy Cooper (former governor) is a strong D recruit. R primary held March 3 — Whatley is the nominee. 20 polls avg D+8.4. Cooper leads Whatley in every poll. Recent: Harper (May '26): D+11; Change Research (May '26, D-sponsored): D+7; Opinion Diagnostics (Apr '26): D+9. TIPP outlier (D+24) excluded. Top Democratic pickup opportunity.

Markwayne Mullin confirmed as DHS Secretary, resigned March 23. Gov. Stitt appointed Alan Armstrong (Williams Companies exec) on March 24; Armstrong signed an oath not to run for the full term. R primary June 16: Rep. Kevin Hern is the frontrunner (Bice opted for House re-election). D primary: Evan Beck, Jim Priest among declared candidates. Deep-red state remains Safe R.
Merkley seeking a fourth term. Oregon has not elected a Republican senator since 2002. Safe D.
Reed seeking re-election to a sixth term. RI has not elected a Republican senator since 2000. Safe D.

Graham only +2 vs generic D and +6 vs Andrews in D-sponsored PPP polls (Nov '25). Avg R+4. Graham is personally unpopular but R+11 PVI keeps this Safe R. Worth monitoring if a strong D candidate emerges.
Rounds seeking a third term. Faces only minor R primary opposition. Won by 31 pts in 2020; deep-red South Dakota (R+27) keeps this Safe R.
Hagerty seeking a second term with Trump's endorsement and nearly $9M raised. No R primary challenger. Deep-red Tennessee (R+26) keeps this Safe R.

R primary runoff (Paxton vs Cornyn) concluded May 24, 2026. 16 polls avg D+2.0. Talarico polls better vs Paxton than vs Cornyn. Barbara Jordan (May '26): near-even in both matchups (Paxton 0, Cornyn R+1). April YouGov/Slingshot showed large D leads but with very low combined shares — likely outliers. Bruising R primary may depress general election turnout. Competitive toss-up regardless of R nominee.
Warner seeking a fourth term. The most notable R challenger, state Sen. Bryce Reeves, withdrew in December 2025. Remaining R field lacks a top-tier recruit. Likely D.
Capito seeking a third term with Trump's endorsement. R primary challenge from convicted Jan. 6 participant Derrick Evans poses no real threat. Deep-red WV (R+30) keeps this Safe R.

Cynthia Lummis announced in December 2025 she will not seek re-election. Rep. Harriet Hageman, endorsed by Lummis, is the frontrunner in the R primary (Aug 18). Deep-red Wyoming (R+35) remains Safe R regardless.

Vacancy election for J.D. Vance's Class III seat, on the November 2026 midterm ballot alongside all other races. Gov. DeWine appointed Jon Husted (former Lt. Gov.) in Jan 2025. Sherrod Brown (lost his OH Class I seat in 2024) running to return to the Senate. Race tightened from Husted +6 (early 2025) to near-even (Brown +4 EMC Feb '26, Brown +2 OnMessage Mar '26), but April polls show Husted reasserting a lead (Echelon R+6, BGSU R+3). 8 polls avg R+2.2. No new polls since April.
